chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who resides in Mecca for a year should perform the deed of the people of Mecca, meaning he should perform the exclusive Hajj (Hajj al-Fard) with the people of Mecca, and whoever stays for less than a year, then for him is that he should perform Tamattu' (the Hajj of Tamattu').

key_terms.الْمُجَاوِرُ: The resident (one who stays in a place for a specific period)
key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعَ: To perform Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are combined with a break in between)
key_terms.يُفْرِدُ الْحَجَّ: To perform the exclusive Hajj (Hajj al-Fard), distinct from Tamattu'

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Hajj al-Fard and Hajj Tamattu' for residents of Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the legal distinction between the Hajj of residents (Ahl al-Qar) and visitors based on a one-year residency threshold in Mecca. It clarifies that those residing for a full year must perform Hajj al-Fard (exclusive Hajj), while those staying less than a year retain the status of pilgrims performing Hajj al-Tamattu'. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the duration of stay as a key determinant for ritual obligations during the Hajj season.
